design.fix: os.fdopen(source, 'rb', closefd=False) inside try/finally os.close(source); the helper stays sole owner of the source fd on every path
design.known_ceiling: an async exception between os.open returning and try entry cannot be closed in pure Python; the mid-walk os.close(directory)/child hand-off is untouched (out of scope)
design.preserved: exact OSError->ValueError translation with cause; non-OSError BaseException propagates by identity; regular-file check; directory walk and directory close; digest; no sweep/GC/retry/rebinding
design.why_not_adopted_flag: io.open closes the raw FileIO itself when a failure happens after FileIO creation (e.g. buffer allocation MemoryError) but leaves the fd open when FileIO init fails first. After a failed fdopen the helper cannot tell which, so close-on-failure either leaks or double-closes (EBADF masking the primary, or closing a reused fd number under threads). closefd=False removes the ambiguity: nothing is adopted, so nothing can be double-closed.
